In [[functional analysis]], the '''girth''' of a [[Banach space]] is the [[infimum]] of lengths of [[centrally symmetric]] [[simple closed curve]]s in the [[unit sphere]] of the space. Equivalently, it is twice the infimum of distances between opposite points of the sphere, as measured within the sphere.<ref name="s67">{{citation
 | last = Schäffer | first = Juan Jorge
 | doi = 10.1007/BF01351519
 | journal = [[Mathematische Annalen]]
 | mr = 0218875
 | pages = 79–82
 | title = Inner diameter, perimeter, and girth of spheres
 | volume = 173
 | year = 1967| s2cid = 116325652
 }}.</ref><ref name="ap">{{citation
 | last = Álvarez Paiva | first = J. C.
 | contribution = Some problems on Finsler geometry
 | doi = 10.1016/S1874-5741(06)80004-X
 | mr = 2194667
 | pages = 1–33
 | publisher = Elsevier/North-Holland, Amsterdam
 | title = Handbook of differential geometry. Vol. II
 | year = 2006}}. See in particular [https://books.google.com/books?id=QUuLp4W1bFAC&pg=PA16 p.&nbsp;16].</ref>

Every finite-dimensional Banach space has a pair of opposite points on the unit sphere that achieves the minimum distance, and a centrally symmetric simple closed curve that achieves the minimum length. However, such a curve may not always exist in infinite-dimensional spaces.<ref name="s67"/>

The girth is always at least four, because the shortest path on the unit sphere between two opposite points cannot be shorter than the length-two line segment connecting them through the origin of the space. A Banach space for which it is exactly four is said to be ''flat''. There exist flat Banach spaces of infinite dimension in which the girth is achieved by a minimum-length curve; an example is the space ''C''[0,1] of continuous functions from the [[unit interval]] to the [[real number]]s, with the [[sup norm]]. The unit sphere of such a space has the counterintuitive property that certain pairs of opposite points have the same distance within the sphere that they do in the whole space.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Harrell | first1 = R. E.
 | last2 = Karlovitz | first2 = L. A.
 | doi = 10.1090/S0002-9904-1970-12643-X
 | journal = Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society
 | mr = 0267383
 | pages = 1288–1291
 | title = Girths and flat Banach spaces
 | volume = 76
 | year = 1970| issue = 6
 | doi-access = free
 }}.</ref>

The girth is a [[continuous function]] on the [[Banach–Mazur compactum]], a space whose points correspond to the normed vector spaces of a given dimension.<ref name="ap"/> The girth of the [[dual space]] of a normed vector space is always equal to the girth of the original space.<ref name="ap"/><ref>{{citation
 | last = Álvarez Paiva | first = J. C.
 | issue = 2
 | journal = American Journal of Mathematics
 | mr = 2214896
 | pages = 361–371
 | title = Dual spheres have the same girth
 | url = https://muse.jhu.edu/journals/american_journal_of_mathematics/v128/128.2paiva.pdf
 | volume = 128
 | year = 2006
 | doi=10.1353/ajm.2006.0015| arxiv = math/0408414
 | s2cid = 201749975
 }}.</ref>
